linkedin_angle.label: Website / Meta Ads lesson
linkedin_angle.brief: Explain one concept about websites or Meta Ads that business owners get wrong (e.g. boost vs real campaigns, what a landing page needs above the fold, why a site loses mobile visitors). Write for business owners anywhere in the world. Teach clearly, with a simple example. No pitch.

post.threads_text:
Your ads are reaching people who will never visit you.

A salon in Anna Nagar doesn't need clicks from Tambaram.
Those people won't travel 20 km for a haircut.

But if your ad is set to all of Chennai, that's where your budget goes.

So pick the area your customers actually come from.
Show them one clear offer.
Make it easy to send a message.

Want us to check your ad setup? Book a free consultation (link in the reply).

post.linkedin_text:
A lot of websites lose people before they even scroll. Not because the business is bad.

It's because the top of the page doesn't answer the basic questions.

The part someone sees before they scroll is called "above the fold". On a phone, that's a very small space. And that's where people decide if they stay or leave.

So what should be there? I think just three things:

1. What you do, in plain words.
Not "We craft experiences". Say "Dental clinic in Velachery" or "Handmade cakes delivered in Dubai".

2. Who it's for.
One line is enough. People want to know "is this for me?"

3. One clear next step.
One button. "Book an appointment" or "Get a quote". Not five buttons fighting each other.

Here's a simple example.

Before: a big slider with a nice photo, a tagline like "Excellence in every detail", and the menu.

After: "Physiotherapy clinic in Anna Nagar for back and knee pain", a line about home visits, and a "Book a session" button.

Same business. But the second one tells the visitor everything in one look.

Actually, a quick test: open your own site on your phone. Without scrolling, can a stranger tell what you do and what to do next? If not, fix that first. Before more ads, before more posts.

This is the kind of thing we look at for clients at Loyara.

#WebDesign #SmallBusiness #DigitalMarketing
